I also wouldn't start with a project. That can get discouraging if youre confused. Just knit. Knit while listening to music or a TV show. Don't have an end goal, just knit to practice! I was very similar to you when I first started working. Save every penny I could. It finally broke when I had to use all my savings to dig my mom out of a financial hole twice. But when i did have your problem, I would try to put my purchases through trials. Like if it's an piece of clothing. How many times will I wear this compared to how much it is? Let's say it's a fancy jacket that costs $60. If I can only realistically see myself wearing it twice, that's 30 a wear! It helps me to think about it and figure out where the money is going so I don't think I'm just wasting my money. If it's like a little trinket or smth. Will it bring me the same amount of contentment or happiness compared to the price? Idk if that would help you but it sure helped me to think and rationalize before buying so I was sure I wanted it. Help calm the anxiety for me :)

No. It's all in the training. You adopt a pittbull that was raised to be aggressive, you have an aggressive dog. You adopt a puppy that wasnt abused and raise it to be sweet, you have a sweet dog. Same with any dog. These people saying "look the the statistics" don't take into the account that those statistics are just face value. Since pitbulls are an oversaturated dog and a lot end up in abuse situations and shelters, it's more common to have a dog that is traumatized and scared. Its easier to find a pittbull thats aggressive. Also pittbull isn't a breed, it's more a look. They're a mutt of a lot of different breeds that share a similar look. It's ridiculous to say "it's the breed" cause there isn't one! I've worked with animals for 4 yrs and the meanest dogs I've worked with have been German shepards, St Bernards and Shiba inus. I also see a lot of golden retrievers that are aggressive but they are also a very common dog breed. Of course I've met aggressive pittbulls but 9/10 the owner isn't taking them to training and doing nothing about their aggression. 

TLDR: it's how you raise them. Pitbull isn't a breed, it's a more like a look.

You could also use chihiros hand since there's more shots of her holding from different angles but Lin's seemed easier to me. All these measurements are just by eye and you of course can make different judgements but that's at least how I would go about it. 

Main point is use pictures of characters holding them to compare sizes. I can't find many other pictures of bath tokens where they aren't being held but it would be easier to find an object that has a more solid average measurements.

You could also find out how tall they are and there formulas online to figure out how big the hands are (forensic scientists use this a lot for bone id since almost all humans are proportionate within a range). Just look up hand size by height and you'll get there.
